comments.note: src/plugins/ledger/index.ts onPostRender — The implementation signature is (output, persona) but the PersonaBuildPlugin interface declares (output, persona, target: TargetType). TypeScript allows narrower parameter lists in implementing methods, so this is not a compile error, but the plugin never has visibility into which target is being rendered. If future logic needs to branch per-target (e.g. different cache keys for vscode vs claude-code), the target parameter will need to be added. Consider adding it now as _target to remain consistent with the interface and make the intent clear.

src/plugins/ledger/index.ts renderedOutputCache — The cache is keyed on persona.name only. When multiple targets are built per persona (vscode + claude-code), onPostRender is called twice, overwriting the first target's cached output with the second. Since onValidate is called once per persona (not once per target), this means the guard always runs against the last-rendered target's output. This is functionally acceptable given the current call order, but the behaviour should be documented in the cache comment (currently the comment says 'each call to onPostRender overwrites the previous entry for the same persona, which is fine' — add 'note_only guard is therefore run against the last-rendered target's output').

src/plugins/ledger/index.ts — warnOnUnknownRole is declared in LedgerPluginOptions with JSDoc @default true but is not wired into the onValidate hook. validateRole always emits a warning. The mismatch between the declared option and the actual behaviour creates a false API promise. Short-term: either remove the option from the public interface (it has no observable effect) or wire it: const { manifestRoles = [], warnOnUnknownRole = true } = options; and pass it to validateRole. Since warnOnUnknownRole = true is the current implicit behaviour, wiring the false branch is a small, safe change.

dist/plugins/ledger/index.js + index.cjs — both dist files contain a duplicate '//# sourceMappingURL=' comment on the last two lines. Confirmed this is a tsup artefact present in all three entry-point bundles (not exclusive to the ledger sub-path). It does not affect runtime correctness or source-map resolution (the first comment wins in most runtimes), but it is unusual output worth tracking. A tsup upgrade or a postbuild dedupe step could clean it up before the 1.0 release.

src/plugins/ledger/role-validator.ts — escapeRegExp is a private module-level function (not exported). This is correct — it is an implementation detail of validateNoteOnlyGuard. However, the same function is likely to be needed by other validators if/when WP-003 introduces additional guard patterns. Consider moving escapeRegExp to a shared utility module (e.g. src/utils/regex.ts) before the 1.0 API freeze to avoid duplicating it across validator files.

src/plugins/ledger/frontmatter-templates.ts — CC_FRONTMATTER_FIELDS is a module-private constant used as a template fragment interpolated into FRONTMATTER_LEDGER_CC via a template literal. The resulting string is byte-identical to the JS original. Pattern is clean and the module doc explicitly explains the inlining rationale. No action needed.

src/plugins/types.ts / src/builders/index.ts — TargetType is exported from both src/plugins/index.ts and src/builders/index.ts, both of which are re-exported by src/index.ts. The canonical definition is in src/plugins/types.ts and the re-export from src/builders/types.ts exists for consumer convenience. This is pre-existing debt (flagged by Developer as constraints.md Known Limitation #3). The dual-path re-export is a type-only collision today, but if TargetType ever gains a value export (const enum or object), the clash would be a hard error. Recommend resolving before 1.0: either remove the re-export from src/builders/index.ts or use an export alias.
